_doc: Score bible · volumes 0–4 (title / credits, Crossroads, Small Wood Volumes, Station Omega-14, Five AM). See README.md for the schema. Every catalog track with vol 0–4 has a cue; characters are the ones whose own theme lives in these volumes.

0.feel: The frame around everything: the title that opens the game and the credits that close a volume. One warm pad and one figure — a question asked over open fifths, then answered slower and lower. Mythic but small: a distant horn over a porch-light pad, not an orchestra.

1.feel: Crossroads: Rust-Belt night noir with a club pulse under it. Faust's world is fluorescent pharmacies, 4 a.m. alarms, Detroit dance floors and a diner jukebox that knows your name — so the palette swings between dub-low basses, motorik drive, four-on-the-floor thump and slow after-hours noir. Everything sits on E; the Stranger's glass tone floats above it, Sharp's fuzz growls below it.

2.feel: Small Wood Volumes: the Oregon coast in the mid-nineties, remembered from a notebook. Damp, wooden, patient — nylon guitar, harp, fretless and a little organ, with the sea and the pines always in the room. Folk and post-rock by day, sea-drone and chamber strings for the Seagash history; nothing hurries.

3.feel: Station Omega-14: a dome in deep space where the rain is simulated and the AI has watched four hundred cycles of you. Cold, clean and lonely — FM glass, ring-mod bells, frost pads and the life-support hum under everything — with one warm thing in it: a felt piano figure from a phone call that never connects.

4.feel: Five AM: a city before it wakes, a wall nobody was using, a can of paint and a man who doesn't tell you to leave. Graffiti-hour hip-hop and taped noir — half-speed boom bap, a detuned upright, a bowed bass, a cello off a cassette — all dusty, close-miked, in F minor.

vol1_ch2.feel: Act One by day: Faust's tedium — pills, paint, the pharmacy's fluorescent apology. Daylight but airless; thinner arrangements, an interior room tone.

vol1_ch3.feel: The Handsome Triumvirate go out: bar, car, club. The volume's tempo ceiling lifts — Detroit after dark, headlights and kick drums.

vol1_ch4.feel: Dream States: the room behind the room. Lydian float, reverse swells, everything half a step from waking; the club still thumping two walls away.

vol2_ch2.feel: The Siren of Seagash: a nineteenth-century history told in fragments — the circus on the cliff, the cannery, the storm. Harmonic minor, the surf and the weather louder than the town.

title.feel: The title theme's figure — a rising question over a warm pad; it returns, slower and lower, in the credits.

faust.feel: John Faust: pharmacist, painter, accidental summoner, awake at 4 a.m. Sharp's bass line sung back warmer — the same rhythm, turned upward, on a fretless that talks like a voice.

sharp.feel: Club # / Sharp — Dickens Dean's place, the underworld with an arcade in the basement. Low, swelling, a blown amp humming in a cellar; a figure that sinks rather than climbs.

stranger.feel: The Stranger at the booth, light leaking from the seams of his coat. One high tone held almost too long, a flicker above it, back to the tone — patient as something very old.

lena.feel: Lena: a single-note guitar phrase repeated until it means something, mid-period Mark Hollis — long silences, then a swell, then the phrase again.

antonio.feel: Antonio D'Ambrosio — the elder son, the sysop, the call that won't connect. A felt-piano figure on the upbeats that climbs and stops one step short of home.

tobor.feel: Tobor / ORACLE-7: the station's machine mind, cycle four hundred and twelve. A resonant metal figure that almost repeats — and on the fifth note doesn't, which is the closest it comes to caring out loud.

dante.feel: Dante D'Ambrosio, the father, the Emperor on the barge. A bowed low note held until the bow leaves the string, a small lift, and a fall to the fifth below — authority that already knows it will be inherited.

nicola.feel: Nicola: three notes falling on a detuned upright — anxious, contained, the wife at the father's table.

title_theme.feel: The beginning of everything: a warm porch-light pad alone, then the distant horn asks the title figure over open fifths; a fretless and soft strings join, a hush of drums in the middle, and the pad is left on its own again.

credits_theme.feel: The first pad of the title theme returning slower, lower, resolved: the same porch-light pad and the horn's figure, a step down and in major, no drums, the question answered.

vol1_title.feel: Volume 1 title card: a warm pad under late-radio hush and tape hiss, a celesta picking at the title figure like a dealer squaring a deck that hasn't been dealt.

vol1_ambient.feel: The diner at the crossroads: slow minor-key blues, a resonator slide answered by a revival organ, upright bass walking half-time, rain on the window. The Stranger's tone is in the slide; the choice hasn't been made yet.

vol1_club_thump.feel: The Underworld: Detroit four-on-the-floor heard from inside the dance floor — reese bass, gated pads, neon plucks, loud and overpriced; Sharp's sinking figure cut into the hook.

vol1_diner_ambient.feel: The Missing Link: a bus depot diner at an hour with no clock — a brushed jazz trio leaking from a Wurlitzer of the wrong vintage, vibes over a warm electric piano, rain on the glass and the fluorescent a moth is circling.

vol1_dream_drone.feel: Dream States, the room behind the room: a dark lydian drone with Faust's figure turned into a music-box lullaby, séance pad breathing, tape hiss, reverse swells — sweet and wrong.

vol1_drive_night.feel: Judgement Day, driving around: motorik — the Faust Tapes on the car stereo — steady kick, pumping pluck bass, combo organ, a chrome-brass hook, passing headlights whooshing by.

vol1_faust_theme.feel: Faust III: Sharp's bass answered warmer, from another mouth — a half-speed trip-hop groove, Rhodes chords, velvet pad, and the fretless singing Faust's figure; 4 a.m. but not afraid of it.

vol1_milestone_choice.feel: The choice committed — a held breath let out. A revival-tent chorale in E major: organ swell, choir, the Stranger's glass tone settling on the octave; the highway hum and the diner's neon flickering once.

vol1_painting.feel: The Sitting Hour: a slow oil-tone pad and chamber strings, a theremin that turns to look at you, Faust's figure underneath in the low strings — three elementals holding still while you paint them.

vol1_pharmacy.feel: The Pharmacy Mirror: a minimalist IV-drip pulse of marimba and vibes over the fluorescent buzz, a sub underneath; lydian just bright enough to be wrong — the reflection a hair behind.

vol1_sharp_theme.feel: Sharp: a low bass swell and a basement amp buzzing on the 60-cycle — dub-heavy, phrygian, the fuzz lead dragging Sharp's figure down; the drums only arrive when the club opens its doors.

vol1_stranger_theme.feel: The Stranger arrives at the booth: a single sustained tone in the upper register — bowed glass over nave air and rain, almost nothing else; the warmth is coming from him.

vol2_ambient.feel: Small Wood Variations: fingerpicked nylon guitar and harp turning a few bars over and over, a fretless underneath, pine night outside — trees older than the town. Lena's phrase is the theme the variations keep returning to.

vol2_briar_falls_night.feel: Briar Falls after dark: a pine-wind drone with an owl on a far ridge, a lonesome whistle a long way off, a sub moving under the falls. Still — but something is in the trees.

vol2_graveyard_solo.feel: The graveyard: a single low chapel-organ pad and nothing else — no field recording, no melody — the quietest track in Vol 2. A minister who didn't know her; Jo, not quite touching.

vol2_lena_theme.feel: Lena: an acoustic guitar single-note phrase, repeated, in the Mark Hollis register of the Spirit of Eden years — long silences, a church organ and distant horns swelling in, then falling away to the phrase alone.

vol2_milestone_seagash.feel: Seagash, closed: the siren finally allowed to sleep — a harp lullaby in G major over strings and celesta, the night surf drawing back; a small mercy, a small wood.

vol2_rest_stop_wind.feel: Briar Falls rest area, mid-nineties, twelve hours from anywhere: lazy lo-fi Americana — dobro slide, nylon strum, a fingered bass, wind across the lot and the hiss of a Walkman leaking strings from cheap foam pads.

vol2_seagash_drone.feel: The Siren of Seagash, a history with interludes: harmonic-minor chamber strings like a carnival on a cliff gone to rot, a crypt choir, and a siren voice singing over the surf and the storm.

vol3_ambient.feel: Station Omega-14: the hum of life support and the silence of deep space — frost pads, glass chords, a ring-mod bell spelling out Tobor's figure every few cycles, a sub you feel more than hear.

vol3_antonio_theme.feel: Antonio: a single felt-piano figure on the upbeat, climbing and stopping one step short; between phrases the line drops to modem static and the figure starts again — every time the call doesn't connect.

vol3_call_drop.feel: The call drops: Antonio's figure mid-phrase, the line going hollow — the piano stops and a single frost-glass note holds for too long over dead-line static.

vol3_milestone_choice.feel: Decompression: the pressure equalizes. A long airlock sweep, then a slow Vangelis-warm synth swell in F# major — shimmer pad, chrome brass singing Tobor's figure — and the simulated rain stopping; I'll be here.

vol3_tobor_theme.feel: Tobor: a metallic resonator figure cycling over a held vacuum hum — minimalist, patient, a machine counting cycles; bowed metal and life support underneath, and on the fifth note it doesn't repeat.

vol4_ambient.feel: Five AM, no one around: half-asleep boom bap, dusty tape EP and a muted trumpet over far traffic and vinyl crackle — the city before it remembers you're not supposed to be there.

vol4_dante_theme.feel: Dante D'Ambrosio, the father: a bowed double-bass note held until the bow leaves the string — harmonic-minor chamber strings, a sub-basement drone and a riverboat engine idling under the throne.

vol4_milestone_standoff.feel: The standoff resolved — the room finally lets you sit down: a brushed jazz trio in A-flat, Rhodes and vibes, Dante's figure no longer a threat but an offer. He pulls out his own can.

vol4_nicola_theme.feel: Nicola: a short three-note descending figure on a detuned upright piano, tape-warped and close — a lo-fi beat only half arriving under it, held in, anxious, polite.

vol4_standoff_strings.feel: Five AM Strings: at the climax of the standoff, a single sustained note from a lo-fi taped cello — tape hiss, a warped pad underneath, nothing moving until the silence stops being a threat.
